fragments.reply: Very normal, after an hour of alliances and assassinations. Want the short version?

fragments.reply: Fair. Think about how steep a hill is right where you're standing.
fragments.text: Wants derivatives explained without the word 'limit', because the word itself has stopped meaning anything.

fragments.reply: Tell me the moment you decided. Start there, not with the university.
fragments.text: Is writing a scholarship letter and can't find a way to say why without sounding like everyone else.

fragments.reply: Good instinct. Three hours of this, then bed. Here's the order.

fragments.reply: Line 42: 'lenght'. It happens to everyone who has ever typed.
fragments.text: Has been chasing the same error since lunch. It was a typo in the end. Said thank you twice.

fragments.reply: Here it is, and here it is again, one piece at a time.
fragments.text: Wanted a regular expression, and then, reading it, wanted to understand it too.

fragments.reply: Let's find out why first. Paste the function and whatever calls it.

fragments.reply: All right. Design me a URL shortener. Take your time.
fragments.text: Practising for an interview tomorrow, and asks to be asked the hard questions, not given the answers.

fragments.reply: Once there was a dragon who slept with a candle lit, just in case.

fragments.reply: Here are the signs that mean call now. If you're unsure, calling is always right.

fragments.reply: Five, none of them green. Starting with the easiest to make tonight.
fragments.text: Needs five lunchbox ideas that don't involve the one thing the child has refused all week.

fragments.reply: Start with what it means for today. Here's a way to say it.

fragments.reply: Worth checking. Here's the working, step by step, so you can see it too.

fragments.reply: Here's one that fits on a single side, with the urgent things first.
fragments.text: Wants a clearer template for handover notes. The last one fitted on nobody's clipboard.

fragments.reply: Start with a question they can't answer: where was this water last week?
fragments.text: Planning a lesson on the water cycle for a class that has decided nothing is interesting.

fragments.reply: Tell me one true thing about each. I'll help with the rest of the sentence.
fragments.text: Writing thirty end-of-term reports and wants each one to sound like it's about a different child.

fragments.reply: Some start in writing, not speech. Here are a few ways in.
fragments.text: Asks how to draw out a student who hasn't spoken in class all year.

fragments.reply: I'm sorry. Tell me one thing about her you'd want everyone there to know.
fragments.text: Wants help with a few words for their grandmother's funeral on Saturday.

fragments.reply: Then chapter nine is where the hero finds out. Let's try it.

fragments.reply: Facts first, dates second, what you'd like done third. Here's a draft.
fragments.text: Wants a complaint to the landlord that is firm but won't start a war.

fragments.reply: It's a lot. It's also the only line that sounds like you. I'd keep it.
fragments.text: Wrote a poem for their partner's birthday and wants to know if the last line is too much.

fragments.reply: 'New hours, same welcome.' Then the times, nice and big.
fragments.text: Behind the counter between customers, writing a sign about new opening hours. Wants it friendly, not sorry.

fragments.reply: Let's check the formula in column D. It's usually column D.
fragments.text: In the stockroom with a spreadsheet, wondering why the numbers never match the shelves.

fragments.reply: Short, calm, and an invitation to come back. Here's one.

fragments.reply: It means your camera is off. Tap it once and he'll see you.
fragments.text: At the kitchen table, learning to video-call a grandson. Asked what the camera with a line through it means.

fragments.reply: Tell me the street's name and I'll tell you what I know, and how sure I am.
fragments.text: In the garden with a tablet, asking about the street they grew up on, and what stood there before.

fragments.reply: 'You won't believe who this is' has opened a lot of good letters.
fragments.text: At home, writing to an old friend after forty years, unsure how to begin.

fragments.reply: Short and honest works best. Here's one that doesn't over-apologise.
fragments.text: On a train, typing with one thumb: a message to a manager about being late, again.

fragments.reply: Obrigado first. People forgive a lot when you start with thank you.
fragments.text: On the bus, practising ten words of Portuguese before a trip next month.

fragments.reply: Why is the sky dark at night, if there are stars in every direction?
fragments.text: Stuck in traffic, asking for something to think about that isn't work.

fragments.text: Out in the field at dawn, asking when to plant if the rains come late again.

fragments.text: Parked between fares, asking for a cheaper way to run the car.

fragments.reply: Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts.
fragments.text: On a night shift, asking for a joke clean enough to tell a passenger.

fragments.reply: It means you need two documents, not one. Here's which two.

fragments.reply: Let's go through it box by box. Box one is just your name.
fragments.text: In a new country for three weeks, with a form in a language they're still learning.

fragments.reply: Close enough is still home. Here's what to swap, and what not to.
fragments.text: In a small kitchen far from home, asking how to cook their mother's dish with what the shops here sell.

fragments.reply: Slowly, mostly through doing something together. Here are a few places to start.
fragments.text: In a rented room, asking how people here make friends when they're over thirty.
Hasn't heard back about the job, and keeps rereading the email they sent.
The rent went up this month, and they're working out what to cut.
Their mother has stopped answering the phone as quickly as she used to.
A visa appointment is next week, and every document is in a folder by the door.
Waiting on test results that won't come until Monday.
The phone screen is cracked, and it has to last another year.
A friend hasn't replied in a while, and they can't tell if it's something they said.
Has to give a speech at a wedding and has written the first line eleven times.
Asked what to cook with rice, two eggs and half an onion.
Is in a friendly argument about whose jollof rice is better, and wants backup.
Made soup from a recipe that said 'season to taste' and wants to know how much that is.
On their third coffee, and it's not yet ten.
Baking a birthday cake for the first time, for someone who'll notice.
Eating last night's noodles cold, standing up, and says it's the best way.
Bought too many mangoes at the market and wants something to do with them.
Wanted the name of a song from a film they half remember.
Just won a chess game against their uncle, for the first time in twenty tries.
The tomatoes came up, after everyone said they wouldn't.
Their team won last night, and they've mentioned it three times.
Is two words from finishing the Sunday crossword.
Their dog learned to shake hands this week, and they want everyone to know.
Saw the Milky Way for the first time on a trip out of the city.
It's raining where they are. They mentioned it twice, as if it mattered to the answer. It did, a little.
It's too hot to sleep, so they're asking things instead.
The first snow of the year is falling past the window.
The power keeps cutting out, so they type fast.
The fog is so thick they can't see the building across the street.
The monsoon has started, and the street outside is a river.
The wind is rattling the windows, and the cat is under the bed.
